stem: An adult with diabetes is prescribed insulin degludec (Tresiba). Which administration instruction is accurate?

options.A: Inject insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily; adults may administer it at any time of day, while the dose should still be individualized to metabolic needs and glucose-control goals.
options.B: Inject insulin degludec only by intravenous infusion because subcutaneous administration is not labeled.
options.C: Administer insulin degludec only immediately before meals because its labeled role is rapid prandial glucose control.
options.D: Convert the displayed units when using U-100 versus U-200 FlexTouch pens because the dose window does not show the actual insulin units.

rationale: Current TRESIBA labeling instructs adults to inject insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily at any time of day and to individualize/titrate the dose based on metabolic needs, blood-glucose monitoring results, and glycemic goals. The label also states not to perform dose conversion between U-100 and U-200 FlexTouch pens because the dose window displays the number of units to deliver. A is correct.
educational_objective: Teach adult insulin degludec administration as once-daily subcutaneous dosing with individualized titration and no manual dose conversion between FlexTouch U-100 and U-200 pens.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_version_date: Current DailyMed prescribing information; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: §2.1 Important Administration Instructions and §2.2 General Dosing Instructions: subcutaneous administration; adults once daily at any time of day; pediatric patients same time every day; individualize/titrate dose; no dose conversion between U-100/U-200 FlexTouch pens.
source_claim_supported: Adults use insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily at any time of day with individualized dosing; FlexTouch U-100/U-200 pens do not require manual dose conversion.

source_original.stem: An adult with diabetes is prescribed insulin degludec (Tresiba). Which administration instruction is accurate?

options.A: Inject subcutaneously once daily; adults may use any time of day, but use the same general daily regimen consistently
options.B: Inject only intravenously because subcutaneous administration is not labeled for insulin degludec
options.C: Give only immediately before meals because insulin degludec is a rapid-acting prandial insulin product
options.D: Convert the displayed units when using U-100 versus U-200 pens because the pen does not show actual units

source_original.rationale: The current TRESIBA label states that adults inject insulin degludec subcutaneously once daily at any time of day. The dose should be individualized, injection sites rotated, and the FlexTouch pen dose counter displays actual units so no concentration conversion is needed. Pediatric patients should receive once-daily dosing at the same time each day.
source_original.source_detail: Section 2.2 General Dosing Instructions: adults inject once daily at any time of day; pediatric patients same time each day; do not perform dose conversion between U-100 and U-200 pens.

correction_summary: Retained key A, removed the vague 'same general daily regimen consistently' phrase and replaced it with exact label language on adult once-daily timing and individualized titration; preserved the no-conversion pen safety point. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed TRESIBA label; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately states route, adult frequency/timing, individualized dose titration and no manual concentration conversion.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because TRESIBA is labeled for subcutaneous administration.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because insulin degludec is a long-acting basal insulin, not a meal-only rapid prandial product.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the label explicitly says not to perform dose conversion between FlexTouch concentrations.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches the adult labeled dosing instructions.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are administration instructions and require product-specific label knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin administration and dose safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current TRESIBA §2.2, all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
